dramatic.state_in: Greg is stable but restless under no-magic restrictions.
dramatic.required_result: Sevren converts stillness into bounded courier work testing practical independence on crutches.
dramatic.state_out: Greg completes useful work without over-solving.
dramatic.ownership: Sevren owns job boundary; Greg owns route and body pacing.

performance.pressure: Greg wants usefulness more than reassurance.
performance.behavior: Sevren offers work casually; Greg bounds logistics, then accepts.
performance.relationship: Trust appears as ordinary work, teasing, and refusal to overhelp.

screenplay: Greg sits still; Sevren treats this as suspicious.
Sevren lays out three delivery slips and defines the job.
Greg tests route, stairs, time, carrying, return and pay.
Greg chooses a longer route over crutch-risky mud.
At a disputed receipt he refuses to solve the merchant problem and returns it annotated.
He completes the job with the boundary intact.

dramatic.state_in: Greg has a promising but ambiguous shaping response.
dramatic.required_result: Hessa tests one unfamiliar localized target without allowing over-interpretation.
dramatic.state_out: A better response appears, but the claim remains narrow.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns test and claims; Greg owns subjective report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants evidence to become a milestone.
performance.behavior: Hessa withholds scoring and asks report before interpretation; Greg stops excitement before it contaminates the attempt.

screenplay: Hessa marks a new point on Greg's hand.
One attempt only changes Greg's tone immediately.
Greg draws and shifts a small altered region toward the target.
He stops before excitement changes the state.
Hessa confirms localized change but rejects an overstrong success label.
Permission remains unchanged.

dramatic.state_in: Greg can initiate alteration but not halt it separately from draw.
dramatic.required_result: Test STOP while underlying draw remains.
dramatic.state_out: Forward change reduces but the patch widens, creating a specific failure.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns stop conditions; Greg owns immediate report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants binary success; Hessa wants a failure map.
performance.behavior: Greg reports unintended widening promptly and accepts a bounded failure.

screenplay: Hessa marks two possible directions.
Greg shapes toward the called line.
Hessa says STOP while telling him to keep draw.
Forward motion reduces but the area widens sideways.
Greg reports spreading; Hessa orders release.
They separate what changed from what he intended.

dramatic.state_in: Greg wants combat training but cannot enter Pessa's normal drill.
dramatic.required_result: Move from generalized desire to a trainable present-tense question.
dramatic.state_out: Pessa identifies the smallest starting point: what changes when Greg simply holds a shield.
dramatic.ownership: Pessa owns drill design; Greg owns desired capability; Alden is pressure, not authority.

performance.pressure: Greg is frustrated at being outside the problem.
performance.behavior: Pessa refuses a premature adaptive system and makes Greg state what he wants today.
performance.relationship: Respect appears as refusal of fake competence and pity.

screenplay: Greg watches movement drills and visibly wants in.
Alden offers himself as opponent; Pessa shuts it down.
Pessa strips Greg's abstract answers until he admits he wants someone to come at him without leaving being the only answer.
She makes him watch one timing question instead of designing a substitute drill.
She hands him a shield for seconds.
The shield changes his center immediately; tomorrow starts there.

dramatic.state_in: Greg has a smallest physical training question.
dramatic.required_result: Expose balance and geometry consequences of shield/crutch movement.
dramatic.state_out: Greg and Pessa identify problems without pretending combat is solved.
dramatic.ownership: Pessa owns geometry; Greg owns movement choices and report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants progress; the body keeps producing unglamorous constraints.
performance.behavior: Pessa changes stakes and her position; Greg increasingly refuses to invent explanations he does not have.

screenplay: Pessa lays irregular stakes.
Greg moves with two crutches, then one, while geometry changes.
Different turns expose late crutch, old support request, acceleration and spatial exposure.
Pessa lets one small hop resolve without catching him.
They rest and resume with narrower questions.
The session ends in better body knowledge, not a system.
